pr_title: Add new skin layer to allow components anchored to the playfield
pr_body:
This has been a common request to cater for rulesets where the playfield changes in shape (ie. osu!mania with different column counts), or for cases where a user has applied playfield scale adjustments.

See commit message attached to 5bd06832d0a4e35bbbd52eea2ffb3970764e6d0e for the major change required to make this work.


https://github.com/ppy/osu/assets/191335/19be5e65-e7fe-4cc0-9e16-44b0ce18a0ee


Addresses #24379.
Closes https://github.com/ppy/osu/issues/22388
pr_comments:
So I've fixed a few more test failures, but the last ones in `SkinDeserialisationTest` I'm not super sure what to do with. They're failing because the ZIP archives with test skins don't have `Playfield.json` inside, thus dying at

https://github.com/ppy/osu/blob/c21167e2ab3b6fd05e54d69537caeca13346c5db/osu.Game/IO/Archives/ZipArchiveReader.cs#L32-L34

But that is curious because skins from before this change continue to work, and I'm pretty sure this failure is _specific to reading skins directly from archives only_. The actual game will use a `DllResourceStore` or a `NativeStorage` underneath, that will just graciously return a null stream, and `Skin` will continue on its merry way.

The `FileNotFoundException` throw in `ZipArchiveReader` is 2016 code, so it's a bit scary to remove it... do we just add blank files to all of the zipped skins or what?
I'm willing to make a lunge and nuke that exception. It doesn't seem to be used anywhere and definitely doesn't match expectations.

issue_context.title: Add per-ruleset skin layout customisation
issue_context.body:
Right now, a skin layout is saved globally for a skin. This doesn't work great for multiple rulesets, where the playfield may be attached to an edge of the screen and cause overlap. Also, in the new "argon" designs, UI elements have already been customised to often be attached to the playfield – this is also the case with classic skins like the osu!mania default.

This epic replaces existing requests for this:
- https://github.com/ppy/osu/issues/12871
- https://github.com/ppy/osu/issues/6124

This could be used to solve issues like:
- https://github.com/ppy/osu/issues/21949
- https://github.com/ppy/osu/issues/20422
- https://github.com/ppy/osu/issues/22362

It would both allow for applying per-ruleset defaults, and give users the option to further customise from those defaults. There should also likely be facilities in the editor to copy full layouts between rulesets (maybe not required if we have clipboard support).
comments:
Pulling out of my recent skin structural write-up for visibility:

Currently we store configuration in individual `json` files, per target container. This likely won't scale well once we add ruleset rules in (and it also makes migrating over version changes harder).

My initial thoughts is that we should move the full skin configuration into a single json structured file, with "layer" objects that container local information as to how/when they should be used. We could then have four of the same layers specified, each with a different ruleset tag to define when they should be used.

This could also allow for the case where multiple rulesets share a layout (ie. there are no ruleset tags), or at very least allow for migration from global to per-ruleset with less fuss.

@frenzibyte looking again at https://github.com/ppy/osu/discussions/20694, I think your first approach is closest to what I had in mind. Did you want to revisit that and see how things play out? I think if you revisit it, also keep in mind what I mentioned in my last comment here. It'll probably be enough to make sure you can easily hook the new structure up to the undo/redo system (#22506).

As an update, frenzi mentioned elsewhere that he's a bit busy at the moment so I'm continuing to work through this.

I've rebased approach 1 at https://github.com/ppy/osu/compare/master...peppy:osu:ruleset-skinning-frenzi-approach-1-rebase?expand=1 and it seems to be working well.
The base work for this has been completed and merged. Remaining tasks are to use this implementation in skin transformers to update the default layouts to match expectations for legacy skins.
